Resource Function Activation and Configuration User Guide

Page iii
Introduction
The
following
document
is
the
user
guide
of
the
REST
API
for
Resource
Function
Activation
and
Configuration
(TMF664).
It
includes
the
model
definition
as
well
as
all
available operations.
This API manages the lifecycle and configuration of Resource Functions, which are abstract
representations of network or IT functions.
Managed Resources
•
ResourceFunction
:
The
core
resource
representing
a
configurable
network
or
IT
function.
•
Heal
: A task resource used to request the healing or restoration of a Resource Function
to a healthy state.
•
Scale
:
A
task
resource
used
to
request
scaling
(e.g.,
scale
out/in)
of
a
Resource
Function.
•
Migrate
: A task resource used to request the migration of a Resource Function from
one location or environment to another.
•
Monitor
:
A
mechanism
used
to
track
activation
and
configuration
of
Services
and
Resources.
Specifically
for
Resource
Functions,
a
Monitor
can
be
used
to
track
the
progress of activation or of other tasks related to resource functions (such as healing,
scaling, migration).
These resources are interconnected. For instance,
Heal
,
Scale
, and
Migrate
operations
act
upon
a
ResourceFunction
.
Monitoring
(
Monitor
)
is
used
to
observe
the
state
changes and progress of these operations.
Supporting Entities
The
API
also
utilizes
supporting
entities
to
describe
the
relationships
and
connectivity
within
Resource
Functions.
One
such
entity
is
ResourceGraph
,
which
focuses
on
the
relationships
and
connectivity
specifically
between
Resource
Functions,
contrasting
with
the more general 'Graph' entity from the Topology API, which describes broader network
topology.
Resource Function Activation and Configuration User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 1
Sample Use Cases
This section outlines typical use cases for the TMF664 Resource Function Activation and
Configuration API.
Use Case 1: Activating a New Firewall Function
An
enterprise
wants
to
deploy
a
new
firewall
function
(a
ResourceFunction
)
for
a
medium-to-large enterprise customer.
1.
Create ResourceFunction
: A POST request to
/resourceFunction
with details of the
firewall (Operating System, MaxTraffic, keywords, IPAddressing features).
2.
Monitor
Activation
:
A
Monitor
resource
is
automatically
created
or
referenced
to
track the activation process.
3.
Check State
: Subsequent GET requests to the
ResourceFunction
or
Monitor
allow
checking the
lifecycleState
and
state
(e.g., from
creating
to
operating
).
Use Case 2: Healing a Failed Resource Function
A deployed firewall function (a
ResourceFunction
) experiences an SLA violation.
1.
Create Heal Operation
: A POST request to
/heal
is made, referencing the problematic
ResourceFunction
and
specifying
the
cause
(e.g.,
"SLA
violation")
and
degreeOfHealing
(e.g., "restoreToStateBeforeFailure").
2.
Monitor Healing
: A
Monitor
resource tracks the progress of the
Heal
operation.
3.
Check
Healing
State
:
GET
requests
to
the
Heal
and
Monitor
resources
show
the
healing
state
(e.g.,
inProgress
,
completed
).
Use Case 3: Scaling a Resource Function
An increase in network traffic requires scaling up the firewall function.
1.
Create
Scale
Operation
:
A
POST
request
to
/scale
is
made,
referencing
the
ResourceFunction
and
specifying
the
scaleType
(e.g.,
"scaleOut"),
aspectId
(e.g.,
"Quick Access Memory"), and
numberOfSteps
.
2.
Monitor Scaling
: A
Monitor
resource tracks the progress of the
Scale
operation.
3.
Check
Scaling
State
:
GET
requests
to
the
Scale
and
Monitor
resources
show
the
scaling
state
.
Resource Function Activation and Configuration User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 2
Use Case 4: Migrating a Resource Function
A planned data center migration requires moving a firewall function to a new location.
1.
Create
Migrate
Operation
:
A
POST
request
to
/migrate
is
made,
referencing
the
ResourceFunction
,
specifying
the
cause
("planned"),
and
providing
new
addConnectionPoint
and
removeConnectionPoint
details.
2.
Monitor Migration
: A
Monitor
resource tracks the progress of the
Migrate
operation.
3.
Check Migration State
: GET requests to the
Migrate
and
Monitor
resources show
the migration
state
.

Page 3
Support of polymorphism and extension
patterns
Support of polymorphic collections and types and schema based extension is provided by
means
of
a
list
of
generic
meta-attributes
that
we
describe
below.
Polymorphism
in
collections
occurs
when
entities
inherit
from
base
entities,
for
instance
a
BillingAccount
and SettlementAccount inheriting properties from the abstract Account entity.
Generic
support
of
polymorphism
and
pattern
extensions
is
described
in
the
TMF
API
Guidelines, Part 2 (TMF630).
The
@type
attribute
provides
a
way
to
represent
the
actual
class
type
of
an
entity.
For
example, within a list of Account instances some may be instances of BillingAccount where
other
could
be
instances
of
SettlementAccount.
The
@type
gives
this
information.
All
resources
and
sub-resources
of
this
API
have
a
@type
attributes
that
can
be
provided
when this is useful.
The @referredType can be used within reference entities (like for instance an AccountRef
object)
to
explicitly
denote
the
actual
entity
type
of
the
referred
class.
Notice
that
in
reference
entities
the
@type,
when
used,
denotes
the
class
type
of
the
reference
itself,
such as BillingAccountRef or SettlementAccountRef, and not the class type of the referred
object.
However
since
reference
classes
are
rarely
sub-classed,
@type
is
generally
not
useful in reference objects.
The @schemaLocation property can be used in resources to allow specifying user-defined
properties of an Entity or to specify the expected characteristics of an entity.
The
@baseType
attribute
gives
a
way
to
provide
explicitly
the
base
of
class
of
a
given
resource that has been extended.

Page 4
RESOURCE MODEL
Managed Entity and Task Resource Models
ResourceFunction resource
A
ResourceFunction
is
a
configurable
network
or
IT
function,
such
as
a
deep
packet
inspector
or
a
firewall.
It
represents
a
behavior
that
transforms
inputs
into
outputs,
independently
of
its
underlying
implementation.
This
API
enables
the
activation,
configuration, and lifecycle management of these functions.
Resource model

administrativeState
A
ResourceAdministrativeStateType.
Value
enumeration
for
the
'resourceAdministrativeState'
of
a
Resource;
the
administrative state attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-
T
M.3701)
represents
permission
to
use
('unlocked')
or
prohibition against using ('locked') the resource imposed
through the management services; it is single valued and
read-write
by
management
functions;
defined
values:
'locked': The resource is administratively prohibited from
performing
services
for
its
users;
'shutdown':
Use
of
the
resource
is
administratively
permitted
to
existing
instances
of
use
only.
While
the
system
remains
in
the
shutting down state the manager may at any time cause
the
managed
object
to
revert
to
the
unlocked
state;
'unlocked':
The
resource
is
administratively
permitted
to
perform
services
for
its
users;
this
is
independent
of
its
inherent operability. ENUMERATED with values:
* locked
* unlocked
* shuttingDown
Resource Function Activation and Configuration User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 11
alarmStatus
A ResourceAlarmStatusType [0..*]. Value enumeration for
the 'resourceAlarmStatus' of a Resource; the alarm status
attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) represents
the
severity
status
of
fault
for
a
resource;
it
is
multi-
valued
and
read-only
by
management
functions,
each
value
represents
an
existing
severity;
defined
values:
'underRepair':
The
resource
is
currently
being
repaired;
'critical': One or more critical alarms indicating a fault have
been
detected
in
the
resource,
and
have
not
been
cleared;
'major':
One
or
more
major
alarms
indicating
a
fault
have
been
detected
in
the
resource,
and
have
not
yet
been
cleared;
'minor':
One
or
more
minor
alarms
indicating a fault have been detected in the resource, and
have
not
yet
been
cleared;
'alarmOutstanding':
One
or
more
alarms
have
been
detected
in
the
resource.
The
condition may or may not be disabling. If the operational
state
is
'enabled',
additional
attributes,
particular
to
the
managed object class, may indicate the nature and cause
of
the
condition
and
the
services
that
are
affected.
ENUMERATED with values:
* underRepair
* critical
* major
* minor
* alarmOutstanding
allocationStatus

ResourceAllocationStatusType.
Values
for
the
'allocationStatus'
of
a
Resource;
for
example:
'available',
'reserved', 'allocated' and 'partiallyAllocated'.

[0..*].
A
list
of

to

autoModification
A Characteristic [0..*]. List of automatic modifications that
can
be
applied
to
a
Resource
Function,
such
as
scaling
actions or automated healing procedures. For example, it
could
describe
parameters
for
auto-scaling
a
firewall
or
auto-healing a network appliance.
Characteristic can be instantiated as
* BooleanArrayCharacteristic
* BooleanCharacteristic
* FloatArrayCharacteristic
* FloatCharacteristic
* IntegerArrayCharacteristic
* IntegerCharacteristic
* NumberArrayCharacteristic
* NumberCharacteristic
* ObjectArrayCharacteristic
* ObjectCharacteristic
* StringArrayCharacteristic
* StringCharacteristic

Page 13
availabilityStatus
A
ResourceAvailabilityStatusType.
Value
enumeration
for
the
'resourceAvailabilityStatus'
of
a
Resource;
the
availability status attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T
M.3701)
represents
the
availability
of
the
resource
for
either carrying service or for being in other states, such as
in
testing;
it
is
single
valued
and
read-only
by
management
functions;
defined
values:
'inTest':
The
resource
is
undergoing
a
test
procedure.
If
the
administrative
state
is
'locked'
or
'shuttingDown',
then
normal users are precluded from using the resource, and
the
controlStatus
attribute
has
the
value
'reservedForTest'.
Tests
that
do
not
exclude
additional
users can be present in any operational or administrative
state
but
the
'reservedForTest'
condition
should
not
be
present;
'failed':
The
resource
has
an
internal
fault
that
prevents
it
from
operating.
The
operational
state
is
'disabled';
'powerOff':
The
resource
requires
power
to
be
applied
and
is
not
powered
on.
The
operational
state
is
'disabled';
'online':
The
resource
is
available
for
use.
The
operational
state
is
'enabled';
'offline':
The
resource
requires a routine operation to be performed to place it
on line and make it available for use. The operation may
be manual or automatic, or both. The operational state is
'disabled'; 'offDuty': The resource has been made inactive
by
an
internal
control
process
in
accordance
with
a
predetermined
time
schedule.
Under
normal
conditions
the
control
process
can
be
expected
to
reactivate
the
resource
at
some
scheduled
time,
and
it
is
therefore
considered
to
be
optional.
The
operational
state
is
'enabled' or 'disabled'; 'dependency': The resource cannot
operate
because
some
other
resource
on
which
it
depends
(i.e.,
a
resource
not
represented
by
the
same
managed
object)
is
unavailable.
The
operational
state
is
'disabled';
'degraded':
The
service
available
from
the
resource is degraded in some respect, such as in speed or
operating
capacity.
Failure
of
a
test
or
an
unacceptable
performance measurement has established that some or
all services are not functional or are degraded due to the
presence
of
a
defect.
However,
the
resource
remains
available
for
service,
either
because
some
services
are
satisfactory or because degraded service is preferable to
Resource Function Activation and Configuration User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 14
category
DEPRECATED
A
String.
Category
of
the
concrete
resource.
e.g
Gold,
Silver for MSISDN concrete resource; NOTE: this property
is misleading and therefore is deprecated.
connectionPoint
A ConnectionPointRef [0..*]. External connection points of
the
Resource
Function.
Each
entry
is
a
reference
to
a
ConnectionPoint resource (a service access point where
inputs and outputs of the function are available). There is
no dedicated TMF API that exposes ConnectionPoint as a
standalone managed resource.
connectivity
A ResourceGraph [0..*]. Internal connectivity of contained
resource functions.
controlStatus
A ResourceControlStatusType. Value enumeration for the
'resourceControlStatus' of a Resource; the control status
attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) indicates
that the resource is under some kind of control; it is single
valued and read-only by management functions; defined
values: 'subjectToTest': The resource is available to normal
users, but tests may be conducted on it simultaneously at
unpredictable
times,
which
may
cause
it
to
exhibit
unusual
characteristics
to
users;
'partOfServicesLocked':
This
value
indicates
whether
a
manager
has
administratively
restricted
a
particular
part
of
a
service
from the user(s) of a resource. The administrative state is
'unlocked'.
Examples
are
incoming
service
barred,
outgoing service barred, write locked by media key, read
locked;
'reservedForTest':
The
resource
has
been
made
administratively unavailable to normal users because it is
undergoing a test procedure. The administrative state is
'locked';
'suspended':
Service
has
been
administratively
suspended
to
the
users
of
the
resource.
The
resource
may
retain
knowledge
of
current
users
and/or
requests
for
usage,
depending
upon
the
managed
object
class
definition, but does not resume performing services until
the
suspended
condition
is
revoked.
The
administrative
state is 'unlocked'. ENUMERATED with values:
* subjectToTest
* partOfServicesLocked
* reservedForTest
* suspended

creationDate
A
DateTime.
The
point
in
time
when
the

endOperatingDate

DateTime.
The
point
in
time
till
the

operating.
externalIdentifier
An
ExternalIdentifier
[0..*].
An
identification
of
this
resource
that
is
owned
by
or
originates
in
a
software
system different from the current system. The structure
identifies
the
system
itself,
the
nature
of
the
resource
within
the
system
and
the
unique
ID
of
the
resource
within the system. It is anticipated that multiple external
IDs can be held for a single resource, e.g. if the resource
passed
through
multiple
systems
on
the
way
to
the
current system.

the provider of the API.

intent

attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) represents
the
planned
and

state
of
a
physical
or
logical
resource;
it
is
single
valued
and
read-write
by
management
functions;
defined
values:
'planned',
'installed', 'pendingRemoval'. ENUMERATED with values:
* planned

* pendingRemoval

operationalState

Value
enumeration
for

Resource;

procedural status attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T

single
valued
and
read-only
by

functions;
defined
values:
'initializationRequired':
The
resource
requires
initialization
to
be
invoked
by
the
manager
before
it
can
perform
its
normal
functions,
and
this
procedure
has
not
been
initiated.
The
manager
may
be
able
to
invoke
such
initialization
through
an
action.
The
operational
state
is
'disabled';
'notInitialized':
The
resource
requires
initialization
before
it
can
perform
its
normal
functions,
and
this
procedure
has
not
been
initiated.
The
resource
initializes
itself
autonomously,
but
the
operational
state
may be either 'disabled' or 'enabled', depending upon the
managed object class definition; 'initializing': The resource
requires
initialization
before
it
can
perform
its
normal
functions, and this procedure has been initiated but is not
yet complete. The operational state may be 'disabled' or
'enabled',
depending
upon
the
managed
object
class
definition;
'reporting':
The
resource
has
completed
some
processing
operation
and
is
notifying
the
results
of
the
operation,
e.g.,
a
test
process
is
sending
its
results.
The
operational state is 'enabled'; 'terminating': The resource is
in a termination phase. If the resource does not reinitialize
itself
autonomously,
the
operational
state
is
'disabled'.
Otherwise, the operational state may be either 'disabled'
or
'enabled',
depending
upon
the
managed
object
class
definition. ENUMERATED with values:
* initializationRequired
* notInitialized
* initializing
* reporting
* terminating

Resources
are

or
non-physical
components
(or
some
combination
of
these)
within
an
enterprise’s
infrastructure
or
inventory.
They
are
typically
consumed
or
used
by
services
(for
example
a
physical
port
assigned
to
a
service)
or
contribute to the realization of a Product (for example, a
SIM
card).
They
can
be
drawn
from
the
Application,
Computing
and
Network
domains,
and
include,
for
example, Network Elements, software, IT systems, content
and
information,
and
technology
components.
A
ResourceSpecification
is
an
abstract
base
class
for
representing
a
generic
means
for
implementing
a
particular
type
of
Resource.
In
essence,
a
ResourceSpecification
defines
the
common
attributes
and
relationships
of
a
set
of
related
Resources,
while
Resource
defines
a
specific
instance
that
is
based
on
a
particular ResourceSpecification.

The CalendarPeriod schema represents a period of time within a calendar, defining various
attributes such as the applicable day, timezone, hour period, and status. It is designed to
capture information about the availability or status of a calendar period, which can be used
in scheduling, booking, or resource allocation applications.

status

period (e.g.: available, booked, etc.).
timeZone
A String. Indication of the timezone applicable to the
calendar information in ISO 8601 timezone: either 'Z' for
UTC or an offset like +02:00 or -05:30.

Endpoint sub-resource fields

connectionPoint
A ConnectionPointRef. Reference to a ConnectionPoint
resource. A ConnectionPoint is modeled as a Resource
that serves as a service access point (SAP) for a Resource
Function, facilitating its interaction with other
components by defining its input and/or output interfaces
(for example, a REST API endpoint, a message queue topic,
or a CORBA operation). There is no dedicated TMF API
that exposes ConnectionPoint as a standalone managed
resource; this reference acts as a lightweight pointer to a
ConnectionPoint resource without embedding its full
implementation details.
isSource
A Boolean. Indicates the directionality of the endpoint
within a connection. If
true
, the endpoint acts as a
source, sending data. If
false
, it acts as a sink, receiving
data. If all endpoints in a multi-point connection are
marked as
true
(sources) and
false
(sinks) respectively,
it implies that specific roles are assigned, e.g., one source
to multiple sinks. If
isSource
is
true
for all participating
endpoints in a connection, it would imply a bidirectional
communication capability for each. Default is
true
.

ResourceSpecificationRef sub-resource fields
Resources are physical or non-physical components (or some combination of these) within
an
enterprise’s
infrastructure
or
inventory.
They
are
typically
consumed
or
used
by
services (for example a physical port assigned to a service) or contribute to the realization
of a Product (for example, a SIM card). They can be drawn from the Application, Computing
and Network domains, and include, for example, Network Elements, software, IT systems,
content
and
information,
and
technology
components.
A
ResourceSpecification
is
an
abstract base class for representing a generic means for implementing a particular type of
Resource.
In
essence,
a
ResourceSpecification
defines
the
common
attributes
and
relationships of a set of related Resources, while Resource defines a specific instance that
is based on a particular ResourceSpecification.

excludedDate

excluded from the Schedule Definition.
id

be locally unique.
monthlyScheduleDayOfMonth
Definition

threshold job.
monthlyScheduleDayOfWeekD
efinition
A MonthlyScheduleDayOfWeekDefinition.

A String. A recurring frequency to run a job within day that
is included in schedule definition, for example: every 5
minutes, 15 minute, 30 minutes, 1 hour.
scheduleDefinitionHourRange
A HourRange [0..*]. A list of time ranges within a specific
day that the schedule will be active on, for example
08:00-12:00, 16:00-19:00.
validFor

weeklyScheduleDefinition
A DayOfWeekRecurrence [0..*]. The weekly schedule is
used to define a schedule that is based on the days of the
week, e.g. a schedule that will be active only on Monday
and Tuesday.

Resource sub-resource fields
Resource is an abstract entity that describes the common set of attributes shared by all
concrete resources (e.g. TPE, EQUIPMENT) in the inventory.
activationFeature
A Feature [0..*]. Configuration features; see TMF664
Resource Function Activation API.
administrativeState
A ResourceAdministrativeStateType. Value enumeration
for the 'resourceAdministrativeState' of a Resource; the
administrative state attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-
T M.3701) represents permission to use ('unlocked') or
prohibition against using ('locked') the resource imposed
through the management services; it is single valued and
read-write by management functions; defined values:
'locked': The resource is administratively prohibited from
performing services for its users; 'shutdown': Use of the
resource is administratively permitted to existing
instances of use only. While the system remains in the
shutting down state the manager may at any time cause
the managed object to revert to the unlocked state;
'unlocked': The resource is administratively permitted to
perform services for its users; this is independent of its
inherent operability. ENUMERATED with values:
* locked
* unlocked
* shuttingDown
Resource Function Activation and Configuration User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 44
alarmStatus
A ResourceAlarmStatusType [0..*]. Value enumeration for
the 'resourceAlarmStatus' of a Resource; the alarm status
attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) represents
the severity status of fault for a resource; it is multi-
valued and read-only by management functions, each
value represents an existing severity; defined values:
'underRepair': The resource is currently being repaired;
'critical': One or more critical alarms indicating a fault have
been detected in the resource, and have not been
cleared; 'major': One or more major alarms indicating a
fault have been detected in the resource, and have not
yet been cleared; 'minor': One or more minor alarms
indicating a fault have been detected in the resource, and
have not yet been cleared; 'alarmOutstanding': One or
more alarms have been detected in the resource. The
condition may or may not be disabling. If the operational
state is 'enabled', additional attributes, particular to the
managed object class, may indicate the nature and cause
of the condition and the services that are affected.
ENUMERATED with values:
* underRepair
* critical
* major
* minor
* alarmOutstanding
allocationStatus
A ResourceAllocationStatusType. Values for the
'allocationStatus' of a Resource; for example: 'available',
'reserved', 'allocated' and 'partiallyAllocated'.
attachment
An AttachmentRef [0..*]. A list of references to
attachments associated with this resource.
Resource Function Activation and Configuration User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 45
availabilityStatus
A ResourceAvailabilityStatusType. Value enumeration for
the 'resourceAvailabilityStatus' of a Resource; the
availability status attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T
M.3701) represents the availability of the resource for
either carrying service or for being in other states, such as
in testing; it is single valued and read-only by
management functions; defined values: 'inTest': The
resource is undergoing a test procedure. If the
administrative state is 'locked' or 'shuttingDown', then
normal users are precluded from using the resource, and
the controlStatus attribute has the value
'reservedForTest'. Tests that do not exclude additional
users can be present in any operational or administrative
state but the 'reservedForTest' condition should not be
present; 'failed': The resource has an internal fault that
prevents it from operating. The operational state is
'disabled'; 'powerOff': The resource requires power to be
applied and is not powered on. The operational state is
'disabled'; 'online': The resource is available for use. The
operational state is 'enabled'; 'offline': The resource
requires a routine operation to be performed to place it
on line and make it available for use. The operation may be
manual or automatic, or both. The operational state is
'disabled'; 'offDuty': The resource has been made inactive
by an internal control process in accordance with a
predetermined time schedule. Under normal conditions
the control process can be expected to reactivate the
resource at some scheduled time, and it is therefore
considered to be optional. The operational state is
'enabled' or 'disabled'; 'dependency': The resource cannot
operate because some other resource on which it
depends (i.e., a resource not represented by the same
managed object) is unavailable. The operational state is
'disabled'; 'degraded': The service available from the
resource is degraded in some respect, such as in speed or
operating capacity. Failure of a test or an unacceptable
performance measurement has established that some or
all services are not functional or are degraded due to the
presence of a defect. However, the resource remains
available for service, either because some services are
satisfactory or because degraded service is preferable to
no service at all. Object specific attributes may be defined
Resource Function Activation and Configuration User Guide
© TM Forum 2026. All Rights Reserved.
Page 46
category
DEPRECATED
A String. Category of the concrete resource. e.g Gold,
Silver for MSISDN concrete resource; NOTE: this property
is misleading and therefore is deprecated.
controlStatus
A ResourceControlStatusType. Value enumeration for the
'resourceControlStatus' of a Resource; the control status
attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) indicates
that the resource is under some kind of control; it is single
valued and read-only by management functions; defined
values: 'subjectToTest': The resource is available to normal
users, but tests may be conducted on it simultaneously at
unpredictable times, which may cause it to exhibit unusual
characteristics to users; 'partOfServicesLocked': This
value indicates whether a manager has administratively
restricted a particular part of a service from the user(s) of
a resource. The administrative state is 'unlocked'.
Examples are incoming service barred, outgoing service
barred, write locked by media key, read locked;
'reservedForTest': The resource has been made
administratively unavailable to normal users because it is
undergoing a test procedure. The administrative state is
'locked'; 'suspended': Service has been administratively
suspended to the users of the resource. The resource may
retain knowledge of current users and/or requests for
usage, depending upon the managed object class
definition, but does not resume performing services until
the suspended condition is revoked. The administrative
state is 'unlocked'. ENUMERATED with values:
* subjectToTest
* partOfServicesLocked
* reservedForTest
* suspended

proceduralStatus
A ResourceProceduralStatusType. Value enumeration for
the 'resourceProceduralStatus' of a Resource; the
procedural status attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T
M.3701) represents a sequence of phases through which
the resource needs to progress; it is single valued and
read-only by management functions; defined values:
'initializationRequired': The resource requires initialization
to be invoked by the manager before it can perform its
normal functions, and this procedure has not been
initiated. The manager may be able to invoke such
initialization through an action. The operational state is
'disabled'; 'notInitialized': The resource requires
initialization before it can perform its normal functions,
and this procedure has not been initiated. The resource
initializes itself autonomously, but the operational state
may be either 'disabled' or 'enabled', depending upon the
managed object class definition; 'initializing': The resource
requires initialization before it can perform its normal
functions, and this procedure has been initiated but is not
yet complete. The operational state may be 'disabled' or
'enabled', depending upon the managed object class
definition; 'reporting': The resource has completed some
processing operation and is notifying the results of the
operation, e.g., a test process is sending its results. The
operational state is 'enabled'; 'terminating': The resource is
in a termination phase. If the resource does not reinitialize
itself autonomously, the operational state is 'disabled'.
Otherwise, the operational state may be either 'disabled'
or 'enabled', depending upon the managed object class
definition. ENUMERATED with values:
* initializationRequired
* notInitialized
* initializing
* reporting
* terminating

resourceSpecification
A ResourceSpecificationRef. Resources are physical or
non-physical components (or some combination of
these) within an enterprise’s infrastructure or inventory.
They are typically consumed or used by services (for
example a physical port assigned to a service) or
contribute to the realization of a Product (for example, a
SIM card). They can be drawn from the Application,
Computing and Network domains, and include, for
example, Network Elements, software, IT systems, content
and information, and technology components. A
ResourceSpecification is an abstract base class for
representing a generic means for implementing a
particular type of Resource. In essence, a
ResourceSpecification defines the common attributes and
relationships of a set of related Resources, while Resource
defines a specific instance that is based on a particular
ResourceSpecification.

.

attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) tracks
whether the resource is currently in use and if it can
accept additional users or not; it is single-valued and
read-only by management functions; defined values: 'idle':
The resource is not currently in use; 'active': The resource
is in use, and has sufficient spare operating capacity to

to provide for additional users at this instant.

administrativeState
A ResourceAdministrativeStateType. Value enumeration
for the 'resourceAdministrativeState' of a Resource; the
administrative state attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-
T M.3701) represents permission to use ('unlocked') or
prohibition against using ('locked') the resource imposed
through the management services; it is single valued and
read-write by management functions; defined values:
'locked': The resource is administratively prohibited from
performing services for its users; 'shutdown': Use of the
resource is administratively permitted to existing
instances of use only. While the system remains in the
shutting down state the manager may at any time cause
the managed object to revert to the unlocked state;
'unlocked': The resource is administratively permitted to
perform services for its users; this is independent of its
inherent operability. ENUMERATED with values:
* locked
* unlocked
* shuttingDown

alarmStatus
A ResourceAlarmStatusType [0..*]. Value enumeration for
the 'resourceAlarmStatus' of a Resource; the alarm status
attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) represents
the severity status of fault for a resource; it is multi-
valued and read-only by management functions, each
value represents an existing severity; defined values:
'underRepair': The resource is currently being repaired;
'critical': One or more critical alarms indicating a fault have
been detected in the resource, and have not been
cleared; 'major': One or more major alarms indicating a
fault have been detected in the resource, and have not
yet been cleared; 'minor': One or more minor alarms
indicating a fault have been detected in the resource, and
have not yet been cleared; 'alarmOutstanding': One or
more alarms have been detected in the resource. The
condition may or may not be disabling. If the operational
state is 'enabled', additional attributes, particular to the
managed object class, may indicate the nature and cause
of the condition and the services that are affected.
ENUMERATED with values:
* underRepair
* critical
* major
* minor
* alarmOutstanding

availabilityStatus
A ResourceAvailabilityStatusType. Value enumeration for
the 'resourceAvailabilityStatus' of a Resource; the
availability status attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T
M.3701) represents the availability of the resource for
either carrying service or for being in other states, such as
in testing; it is single valued and read-only by
management functions; defined values: 'inTest': The
resource is undergoing a test procedure. If the
administrative state is 'locked' or 'shuttingDown', then
normal users are precluded from using the resource, and
the controlStatus attribute has the value
'reservedForTest'. Tests that do not exclude additional
users can be present in any operational or administrative
state but the 'reservedForTest' condition should not be
present; 'failed': The resource has an internal fault that
prevents it from operating. The operational state is
'disabled'; 'powerOff': The resource requires power to be
applied and is not powered on. The operational state is
'disabled'; 'online': The resource is available for use. The
operational state is 'enabled'; 'offline': The resource
requires a routine operation to be performed to place it
on line and make it available for use. The operation may be
manual or automatic, or both. The operational state is
'disabled'; 'offDuty': The resource has been made inactive
by an internal control process in accordance with a
predetermined time schedule. Under normal conditions
the control process can be expected to reactivate the
resource at some scheduled time, and it is therefore
considered to be optional. The operational state is
'enabled' or 'disabled'; 'dependency': The resource cannot
operate because some other resource on which it
depends (i.e., a resource not represented by the same
managed object) is unavailable. The operational state is
'disabled'; 'degraded': The service available from the
resource is degraded in some respect, such as in speed or
operating capacity. Failure of a test or an unacceptable
performance measurement has established that some or
all services are not functional or are degraded due to the
presence of a defect. However, the resource remains
available for service, either because some services are
satisfactory or because degraded service is preferable to
no service at all. Object specific attributes may be defined

controlStatus
A ResourceControlStatusType. Value enumeration for the
'resourceControlStatus' of a Resource; the control status
attribute (defined by ITU-T X.731/ITU-T M.3701) indicates
that the resource is under some kind of control; it is single
valued and read-only by management functions; defined
values: 'subjectToTest': The resource is available to normal
users, but tests may be conducted on it simultaneously at
unpredictable times, which may cause it to exhibit unusual
characteristics to users; 'partOfServicesLocked': This
value indicates whether a manager has administratively
restricted a particular part of a service from the user(s) of
a resource. The administrative state is 'unlocked'.
Examples are incoming service barred, outgoing service
barred, write locked by media key, read locked;
'reservedForTest': The resource has been made
administratively unavailable to normal users because it is
undergoing a test procedure. The administrative state is
'locked'; 'suspended': Service has been administratively
suspended to the users of the resource. The resource may
retain knowledge of current users and/or requests for
usage, depending upon the managed object class
definition, but does not resume performing services until
the suspended condition is revoked. The administrative
state is 'unlocked'. ENUMERATED with values:
* subjectToTest
* partOfServicesLocked
* reservedForTest
* suspended

completed:

to

much
of

as

even
if
some
parts
fail,
while
'atomic'
means
the
entire
migration
operation
must
succeed
or
fail
as
a
single,
indivisible
unit,
ensuring
full
consistency. ENUMERATED with values:
* bestEffort
* atomic

Function,

by

and/or
output

(for

dedicated TMF API that exposes ConnectionPoint as a standalone managed resource; this
reference acts as a lightweight pointer to a ConnectionPoint resource without embedding
its full implementation details.

Remove an Entity

Entity

execute Task Resources
Other Request Methods
POST on TASK Resource
GET and POST must not be
used to tunnel other request
methods.

API NOTIFICATIONS
For
every
single
of
operation
on
the
entities
use
the
following
templates
and
provide
sample REST notification POST calls.
It is assumed that the Pub/Sub uses the Register and UnRegister mechanisms described in
the REST Guidelines reproduced below.
Register listener
POST /hub
Description
Sets
the
communication
endpoint
address
the
service
instance
must
use
to
deliver
information about its health state, execution state, failures and metrics. Subsequent POST
calls will be rejected by the service if it does not support multiple listeners. In this case
DELETE /api/hub/{id} must be called before an endpoint can be created again.
Behavior
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 409 if request is not successful.
Usage Samples
Here’s an example of a request for registering a listener.
Request
POST /api/hub
Accept: application/json
{
 
"callback": "http://in.listener.com"
}
Response
201
Content-Type: application/json
Location: /api/hub/42

Unregister listener
DELETE /hub/{id}
Description
Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub..
Behavior
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 204 if the request was successful.
Returns HTTP/1.1 status code 404 if the resource is not found.
Usage Samples
Here’s an example of a request for un-registering a listener.
Request
DELETE /api/hub/42
Accept: application/json
Response
204
Publish Event to listener
POST /client/listener
Description
Clears the communication endpoint address that was set by creating the Hub.
Provides
to
a
registered
listener
the
description
of
the
event
that
was
raised.
The
/client/listener url is the callback url passed when registering the listener.
